services.aliasVaultInstructionsPart1: Import your previously created AliasVault backup.
services.bitwardenDescription: Import passwords from your Bitwarden vault
services.bitwardenInstructionsPart1: In order to import your Bitwarden vault, you need to export it. You can do this by logging into your Bitwarden account, going to the 'Tools' menu and selecting 'Export vault'.
services.chromeDescription: Import passwords from your Chrome Password Manager
services.chromeInstructionsPart1: In order to import your Chrome Password Manager, you need to export it as a CSV file. You can do this by logging into your Chrome browser, going to the 'Settings' menu > 'Password and AutoFill' > 'Google Password Manager'. Then click on 'Export passwords'.
services.dashlaneDescription: Import passwords from your Dashlane account
services.dashlaneInstructionsPart1: In order to import your Dashlane passwords, you need to export it as a CSV file. You can do this by logging into your Dashlane account, going to the 'Account' > 'Settings' menu and selecting 'Export to CSV'.
services.dashlaneInstructionsPart2: Note: the .zip file you download will contain a "credentials.csv" file. You need to unzip the archive first, and then upload the "credentials.csv" CSV file below.
services.dropboxInstructionsPart1: In order to import your Dropbox Passwords, you need to export them as a CSV file. You can do this by opening Dropbox Passwords, going to 'Account' > 'Export' (to .CSV).
services.edgeDescription: Import passwords from your Microsoft Edge Password Manager
services.edgeInstructionsPart1: In order to import your Microsoft Edge passwords, you need to export them as a CSV file. You can do this by going to Menu > Settings > Password and autofill > Microsoft Password Manager > ... > Export passwords.
services.enpassInstructionsPart1: In order to import your Enpass passwords, you need to export them as a CSV file. You can do this by opening Enpass, going to 'Menu' > 'File' > 'Export' and selecting 'CSV file (.csv)'.
services.firefoxDescription: Import passwords from your Firefox Password Manager
services.firefoxInstructionsPart1: In order to import your Firefox passwords, you need to export it as a CSV file. You can do this by opening your Firefox browser, going to menu > 'Passwords'. Then click on the menu icon in the top right corner and select 'Export passwords'.
services.genericCsvDescription: Import credentials using a template CSV format
services.genericCsvInstructionsPart1: Is the password manager you are using not supported? You can always import your credentials into AliasVault using a generic CSV template format instead.
services.genericCsvStep2: Open it in a spreadsheet program (Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, etc.)
services.genericCsvStep3: Fill in your credentials (replace the example data)
services.genericCsvStep4: Save as CSV format and upload it below
services.genericCsvTemplateDownloadError: Failed to download CSV template. Please try again.
services.keePassInstructionsPart1: In order to import your KeePass vault, you need to export it as a CSV file. You can do this by going to the 'File' menu and selecting 'Export' (to CSV).
services.keePassXCInstructionsPart1: In order to import your KeePassXC vault, you need to export it as a CSV file. You can do this by going to the 'Database' menu and selecting 'Export' (CSV File).
services.lastPassDescription: Import passwords from your LastPass vault
services.lastPassInstructionsPart1: In order to import your LastPass vault, you need to export it as a CSV file. You can do this by logging into your LastPass account, going to 'Advanced Options' in the left sidebar and selecting 'Export' > 'LastPass CSV File'.
services.nordPassInstructionsPart1: In order to import your NordPass passwords, you need to export them as a CSV file. You can do this by opening the NordPass app or web vault, going to 'Settings' > 'Export Items', and selecting the CSV format.
services.onePasswordInstructionsPart1: In order to import your 1Password vault, you need to export it. You can do this by logging into your 1Password account in the 1Password 8 desktop app (Windows / MacOS / Linux), going to the 'File' menu and selecting 'Export'.
services.protonPassInstructionsPart1: In order to import your Proton Pass vault, you need to export it. You can do this in the Proton Pass browser extension by going to 'Settings' > 'Export'.
services.roboformInstructionsPart1: In order to import your RoboForm passwords, you need to export them as a CSV file. You can do this by opening RoboForm, going to 'RoboForm' menu > 'Options' > 'Account & Data' > 'Export' and selecting CSV format.
services.strongboxInstructionsPart1: In order to import your Strongbox vault, you need to export it as a CSV file. You can do this by going to the 'File' menu and selecting 'Export Database' (to CSV).
services.uploadInstructions: Once you have exported the file, you can upload it below.

settings.exportSectionDescription: Export your vault data to a CSV file. This file can be used as a back-up and can also be imported into other password managers.
settings.exportWarning:
Warning: Exporting your vault to an unencrypted file will expose all of your passwords and sensitive information in plain text. Only do this on trusted devices and ensure you:

• Store the exported file in a secure location
• Delete the file when you no longer need it
• Never share the exported file with others

Are you sure you want to continue with the export?

welcome.extensionsAppsTipContent: Install the AliasVault browser extension and mobile app to create aliases and autofill forms directly from your browser and smartphone.
welcome.howItWorksIntro: When you need to sign up for a new service:
welcome.howItWorksStep1: AliasVault generates a random identity with a secure private email address
welcome.howItWorksStep2: Use this information to sign up for the service
welcome.howItWorksStep3: Received emails show up in this app and can be opened in your browser
welcome.howItWorksStep4: Your real email address and other personal information stay private
welcome.masterPasswordTipContent: Your master password is required to decrypt your vault. Never share it with anyone and store it in a secure location. Warning: If you lose your master password, your data cannot be recovered - not even by our team.
welcome.readyToStartMessage: Now that you know how AliasVault works, let's create your first secure identity!
welcome.twoFactorTipContent: Two-factor authentication adds an extra layer of security to your account. It requires you to enter a code from your authenticator app or provide a recovery code before your encrypted vault can be accessed.
welcome.twoFactorTipTitle: Enable Two-Factor Authentication In Security Settings
welcome.welcomeMessage: Your vault has been successfully created! Protect your online privacy by creating unique aliases for each service you sign up for. Let's learn how AliasVault works and then create your first secure alias.
